courses.name: Legal & Ethical Issues in Sustainability
taughtSkills: applying ethical reasoning to business decision-making
analyzing anti-bribery and corruption laws (e.g., FCPA, UK Bribery Act)
evaluating corporate sustainability/ESG and governance practices
designing elements of an effective compliance program for risk management
stakeholder management
courses.levelNote: No prerequisite is listed for this course, so it is entry-level (1000).

evidence.quote: This course will require students to understand broad business sustainability issues and to apply ethical reasoning processes to decision making. ... Initiatives & laws such as Anti-Bribery and Corruption (e.g., the United States Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA), the UK Bribery Act), the Sustainable Development Goals, the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the United Nations Global Compact will be considered... We will examine the elements of an effective compliance program as a tool to risk management.

courses.name: Decision Making with Programming & Analytics
taughtSkills: managing and preparing data for analysis
writing Python code for customized business analytics solutions
integrating statistical libraries for data analysis
constructing visuals and reports to communicate analytics outcomes
courses.levelNote: No prerequisite is listed; the description calls it 'an introductory course... for students who have no programming background', so 1000-level.

evidence.quote: This course will equip students with the ability to write customized solutions to inform business decision, integrate statistical libraries for data analysis, and construct visuals or reports for business understanding. ... We utilize Python language as the medium of learning because it is one of the most in-demand coding language and its user-friendly syntax is well suited for the beginner level.

courses.name: Financial Management
taughtSkills: understanding core financial principles and concepts
applying analytical tools for financial decision-making
foundational finance knowledge for business and accounting students
preparing for advanced finance coursework (corporate finance, financial markets, investments)
courses.levelNote: No prerequisite is listed; text states 'This is a first course in finance and is compulsory for all business and accounting students,' confirming entry-level (1000).

evidence.quote: This course aims to provide business and accounting students with a broad understanding of all the important financial principles, concepts, and analytical tools. This is a first course in finance and is compulsory for all business and accounting students.

courses.name: Statistics & Analysis
taughtSkills: statistical inference under uncertainty
programming in R for statistical analysis
probability modeling
regression analysis
simulation analysis
courses.levelNote: No prerequisite is listed, and the description frames this as an introductory statistics course, so 1000-level.

evidence.quote: This course introduces the concepts and methods of statistical inferences: the process of inferring unknowns under uncertainty. Students of this course will also learn programming skills in the R environment for basic statistical analyses. ... Section 1 covers elements of probability models. Section 2 covers the basic theories in statistical inferences. Section 3 introduces the basic of two powerful and widely used analytic tools: regression and simulation analysis.

courses.name: Business Law
taughtSkills: legal methodology and principles of business law
contract formation, terms, breach and termination
law of agency
business organisations and torts fundamentals
analyzing how commercial law and business practices inter-relate
courses.levelNote: No prerequisite is listed, and the course is described as providing a 'solid foundation' on legal methodology, so 1000-level.

evidence.quote: this course provides a solid foundation on the legal methodology and the main principles of law relating to business transactions. A number of topics will be discussed in this course ranging from the formation of contracts, terms of a contract, breach and termination of a contract, law of agency, business organisations and torts.

courses.name: Business Valuation: From Theory to Practice
taughtSkills: conducting business valuation using recognized approaches and methods
applying international valuation standards (IVSC)
valuing businesses and equity for transaction purposes
understanding valuation terms, definitions, and premises of value
analyzing discounts/premiums in valuing public and private companies
courses.levelNote: Prerequisite is a single intro-level accounting course (AC1102 OR AD1101 OR AC1104 OR AD1102), so 2000-level.

evidence.quote: This course provides students with the conceptual background, practical skills and knowledge that are necessary to conduct business valuation in the marketplace. ... it will provide an insight into the international valuation standards promulgated by the International Valuation Standards Council (IVSC) and in-depth coverage on the valuation process ... A detailed study of the various valuation approaches and methods commonly used to value business and equity for transactions purposes will also be carried out. ... the course will also address the challenges encountered by valuers relating to discounts/ premiums and valuation of public listed entities and private companies.

courses.name: Forensic Accounting & Fraud Investigation
taughtSkills: fraud investigation methodology
IT forensics and social media tracing for evidence examination
analyzing fraudulent schemes (financial statement, cash receipt/disbursement, defalcation, cybercrime)
interviewing and interrogation techniques
understanding the role of an expert witness
courses.levelNote: Prerequisite is a single intro-level accounting course (AC1102 OR AD1101 OR AC1104 OR AD1102), so 2000-level.

evidence.quote: The course provides an understanding of white collar crimes in Singapore by analyzing real case studies of major crimes. Students will be taught the investigation methodology in the detection of fraud and the use of information technology forensics and social media tracing to examine documents and evidence within the Singapore legal, regulatory and professional rule-based environment. Various fraudulent schemes will be examined including financial statements, cash receipt, cash disbursement, defalcation and cybercrimes. Finally, the course teaches students effective interviewing and interrogation techniques, and the role of an expert witness.

courses.name: Strategic Management
taughtSkills: analyzing external and internal environments of a firm
formulating and executing business strategy
evaluating sources of superior firm performance using conceptual frameworks
incorporating corporate governance considerations into strategy
critically analyzing business issues from a strategic perspective
courses.levelNote: Prerequisite requires two prior 1000-level courses together (AB1501 & AB1601), and the description targets 'final-year' students, indicating a deeper chain (3000).

evidence.quote: The purpose of the Strategic Management Course is to develop your knowledge and skills to identify and evaluate the sources of superior firm performance through using conceptual frameworks. You will learn to analyze the external and internal environments of the firm, formulate and execute different types of strategies with the consideration of good corporate governance. This course is appropriate for final-year accounting and business students who have already taken entry-level courses in accounting ratio analyses, organizational behaviour and marketing.

courses.name: Sustainability Reporting
taughtSkills: preparing and interpreting sustainability/integrated reports
applying ESG reporting standards (TCFD, GRI, IR, SASB, ISSB)
measuring and communicating corporate sustainability performance
understanding mandatory sustainability reporting requirements for listed companies
courses.levelNote: Prerequisite is AC3104, itself a course with prerequisites, so this is a deeper chain (3000).

evidence.quote: corporations both small and large are reporting their sustainability (or Environmental, Societal and Governance [ESG]) efforts and performance. In many countries, sustainability reporting is a mandatory requirement, especially for listed companies. ... The focus of this course will be on both preparing and interpreting sustainability and integrated reports. This course covers some of the key existing standards used for environmental, social and governance (ESG) such as Task Force on Climate Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), Global Reporting Initiatives (GRI), Integrated Reporting (IR), Sustainability Reporting Standards Board (SASB) and International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB).
